summary.intent: Implement a comprehensive SDK-based E2E and load testing strategy for CipherBox, replacing browser-automation Playwright tests with direct SDK calls for faster, more reliable test coverage.
summary.outcome: Created two new workspace packages (tests/sdk-e2e with 83 passing tests across 10 suites, and tests/load with 5 scenarios), two CI workflows, a TESTING_STRATEGY.md doc, and a todo for the api-client singleton refactor. All 83 SDK E2E tests pass against a local stack.

repo: The API ThrottlerGuard uses 10 req/s and 100 req/min limits which block rapid SDK test suites; rate limiter must be relaxed for test environments via NODE_ENV check
NODE_ENV in .env file takes precedence over shell env vars when NestJS ConfigModule loads it — must edit .env directly, not just pass NODE_ENV=test to the shell

setApiClientConfig is a module-level singleton in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts because orval generates standalone functions that import customInstance — it's a code-gen pattern, not a technical requirement
Multi-account SDK tests must call setApiClientConfig before each operation to switch accounts, and later tests can be contaminated if they don't re-set the singleton
The invite claim DTO has @MinLength(258) on encryptedKey (ECIES ciphertext is at least 129 bytes = 258 hex chars) — dummy test keys must use real wrapKey() output
The API returns wrapped share keys as hex strings but unwrapKey() expects Uint8Array — needs hexToBytes() conversion before passing to crypto functions
CipherBoxClient.getFolderTree() is the public API for accessing folder state — (client as any).folderTree casts should not be used in tests
The Playwright load test (tests/e2e/tests/load-test.spec.ts) runs ~70 operations per client across 5 browser contexts against staging — useful workload reference
POST /auth/test-login has its own stricter throttle separate from the global ThrottlerModule config
pnpm-workspace.yaml has three groups: apps/*, packages/*, tests/* — new test packages go under tests/ and must be added to pnpm-workspace.yaml

code.finding: Module-level singleton for API config; no deep technical reason for this design — orval can be configured to accept per-instance axios instances instead
Gold standard pattern: test-login → initializeVault → encryptVaultKeys → setApiClientConfig → new CipherBoxClient → registerFolder
ThrottlerModule config — added NODE_ENV=test conditional to set ttl=60000/limit=10000 for test environments
CipherBoxClient has no browser/React/Zustand dependencies — pure TypeScript/ESM, suitable for Node.js test environments
switchTo() pattern required before each IPNS operation in multi-account tests due to api-client singleton; operations must run serially

workflow: Running TypeScript type-check (tsc --noEmit) after writing test files catches issues like unused imports (noUnusedLocals), wrong types, and rootDir violations before running tests
When extracting shared code between two packages, check if tsconfig rootDir restrictions prevent cross-package imports — may need to adjust or use a shared package instead
For large implementation sessions, parallel Write tool calls for independent files significantly speeds up file creation
1Password SSH agent for commit signing times out in background agent subprocesses — commits from agent may hang; user must run from terminal or retry
Load test metrics aggregation should use getReadonlySamples() to avoid unnecessary array copies when computing statistics
The 'simplify' skill effectively catches: cross-package code duplication, repeated aggregation blocks, unnecessary type casts when public APIs exist, and shared fixture inefficiencies

friction: 1Password SSH agent unavailable in background Bash subprocesses causing commit signing to hang indefinitely — required manual user intervention or retries
NODE_ENV=test passed to shell was silently overridden by .env file contents, making the ThrottlerModule change appear to have no effect until .env was edited directly
API ThrottlerGuard (10 req/s, 100 req/min) blocked single test suites even when running one at a time — required API code change before tests could run
Invite claim DTO @MinLength(258) validation rejected dummy test keys — error message (400) didn't clearly indicate the key was too short
The explore subagent completed after the main implementation was already done — background agent timing meant its findings arrived too late to be useful
TypeScript rootDir restriction in tests/load/tsconfig.json prevented importing from tests/sdk-e2e — required tsconfig adjustment
open_items: Refactor api-client to instance-scoped axios instead of module-level singleton (todo filed: .planning/todos/pending/2026-03-22-refactor-api-client-from-singleton-to-instance-scoped-axios.md) — eliminates switchTo() hack, cross-suite contamination, and enables true parallel clients

Implement throttle bypass header (option 2) for load tests against staging — a secret-verified X-Throttle-Bypass header so load tests can run without throttle interference while production limits remain intact
Load tests against production cluster not yet designed — staging load tests answer single-node capacity questions only; a separate strategy needed for testing horizontal scaling effectiveness
Add 'throttle validation' scenario to load tests that deliberately does NOT bypass, to verify the throttler itself works correctly under load
TESTING_STRATEGY.md committed to PR but not yet reviewed by team — documents rate limiting tiers, horizontal scaling implications, k6 rationale, and singleton caveats
